reason: This Genesis 24 narrative demonstrates multiple instances of characters freely expressing their views and concerns. The servant actively voices doubts to Abraham about whether the woman will consent to travel (וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלָיו הָעֶבֶד אוּלַי לֹא־ תֹאבֶה הָאִשָּׁה), asks direct questions of Rebekah (וַיֹּאמֶר בַּת־ מִי אַתְּ), and freely reports his purpose and God's guidance to Laban and Bethuel. Rebekah is explicitly consulted on whether to depart (וַיִּקְרְאוּ לְרִבְקָה וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֵלֶיהָ הֲתֵלְכִי עִם־ הָאִישׁ הַזֶּה), and she directly expresses her consent. Throughout the narrative, dialogue and discussion are encouraged, decisions are discussed with multiple parties, and people ask questions freely. The text shows no discouragement of expressing views; rather, it demonstrates active dialogue and consultation.
